newsitem.title: USA: Florida citrus groves in very good condition- FASS.
newsitem.headline: Florida citrus groves in very good condition- FASS.

text.p: Conditions were "very good" throughout Florida's citrus belt in the week ended September 8, with new crop fruit continuing to make good progress," the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS) said.

Rainfall during the week was spotty, with some regions reporting locally heavy thunderstorms while some growers in the interior of the citrus belt ran irrigation equipment," FASS said in its weekly release.
New growth was starting to harden up, FASS said, with only a few young trees showing new foliage.
The first crops of the 1996/97 have been picked, and the fruit is in two packing houses in Polk County. The Ambersweet oranges will be packed and shipped September 10-11, FASS said.

FASS said caretakers are cutting cover crops and applying fall herbicides to weeds that have grown aggressively in the past several weeks. Fall sprays, fertilizations and limes are being applied to all areas. Dead tree removal and some resetting continued, they added.
